Definition: from G303 and a form of the alternate of G138; properly, to use up, i.e. destroy:--consume.
BiblicalUsage: The word means to use up, to consume: James and John ask whether they should command fire to come down from heaven and consume the Samaritans, even as Elijah did, and Paul warns the Galatians that if they bite and devour one another, they should take heed that they are not consumed one of another. Fire from heaven in the one verse, and a church eating itself alive in the other.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for consuming carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the warning — the disciples wanted fire on Samaria, and Paul warns that a biting church will be consumed by its own teeth.
